title: How a car works: from bang to wheels
summary: Find out how tiny bangs inside a car's engine end up turning its wheels.
objective: Explain how a petrol engine's four steps make a push, and how that push reaches the wheels.

hook.prompt: What makes a petrol car's wheels go round?

options.text: Lots of tiny bangs inside the engine, many times a second
A big fan inside the engine that blows the car along
options.feedback: Cars do have a fan, but it only keeps the engine cool. It doesn't push the car.

options.text: Petrol shooting out of the back, like a rocket
options.feedback: That's how rockets move. In a car, the petrol stays inside and gets used up in the engine.

options.text: A battery, like the one in a toy car
options.feedback: Petrol cars do have a battery, but it mostly starts the engine and runs things like the lights.

hook.explanation: A petrol engine makes lots of tiny bangs every second. Each bang gives a push, and all those pushes add up to move the car.

bricks.title: Suck, squeeze, bang, blow
bricks.body: A petrol car's engine has metal tubes called **cylinders**. Inside each one, a **piston** slides up and down. Over and over, four steps happen. **Suck:** the piston slides down and pulls in fuel and air. **Squeeze:** it slides up and squashes them. **Bang:** the **spark plug** makes a tiny spark. The fuel burns with a bang and shoves the piston down hard. **Blow:** the piston slides up and pushes the used-up gas out of the exhaust pipe.

term.definition: A metal plug that slides up and down inside a cylinder. The bang pushes it down.

visual.html:

visual.alt: An engine cylinder: fuel and air pipe on one side, gas-out pipe on the other, a spark plug on top, and a piston inside joined to a wheel below.

bricks.prompt: Put the engine's four steps in order, starting with fuel and air coming in.

items.text: Fuel and air are pulled into the cylinder
The piston squashes the fuel and air
A spark makes the fuel burn and shove the piston down
Used-up gas is pushed out of the exhaust pipe

bricks.hint: Remember the four words: suck, squeeze, bang, blow.
bricks.explanation: Suck, squeeze, bang, blow: fuel and air come in, get squashed, burn with a bang, then the used-up gas goes out. Then it all starts again.

bricks.prompt: Tap the part that makes the spark.
bricks.hint: It sits on top of the cylinder, right above the piston.
bricks.explanation: The **spark plug** sits on top of the cylinder. Its tiny spark sets the squashed fuel burning.

bricks.prompt: Which of the four steps actually pushes the car along?

options.feedback: Suck only pulls fuel and air in. Nothing is burning yet, so there's no push.
Squeeze gets the fuel and air ready. The piston is doing the squashing here, not being pushed.
Blow just clears out the used-up gas so the next round can start.

bricks.hint: Which step shoves the piston down hard?
bricks.explanation: In **Bang**, the burning fuel shoves the piston down hard. That shove is the push that moves the car. The other three steps get ready for the next bang.

bricks.prompt: Which step is this picture showing?

visual.html: ↑
visual.alt: The engine with an arrow showing the piston moving up, and grey puffs of gas coming out of the exhaust pipe.

options.feedback: In Suck, the piston slides down and fuel and air come in. Here the piston is going up.
The piston goes up in Squeeze too, but nothing leaves: the fuel and air get squashed. Here gas is coming out.
In Bang, the spark fires and the piston gets shoved down. Here it's moving up.

bricks.hint: Look at which way the piston moves and where the grey puffs are going.
bricks.explanation: The piston is moving up and used-up gas is puffing out of the exhaust pipe. That's **Blow**.

bricks.title: From the piston to the wheels
bricks.body: The piston is joined to a bent rod called the **crankshaft**. Each bang pushes the piston down, and that turns the crankshaft round, just like your legs push bike pedals round. The spinning crankshaft passes its turn to the **gearbox**, and the gearbox passes it to the wheels. Like bike gears, **low gears** give lots of push for starting and climbing hills. **High gears** are for going fast on a flat road.

term.definition: A bent rod that the pistons push round, like bike pedals. It turns their up-and-down push into a spin.

visual.html:

visual.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: Piston, then Crankshaft, then Gearbox, then Wheels.

bricks.prompt: On a bike, your legs push the pedals round. Which car part do the pistons push round, like those pedals?

options.feedback: The wheels do turn, but last. The spin goes through the gearbox before it reaches them.
The gearbox gets its spin from the crankshaft and passes it on. The pistons don't push it directly.
The spark plug makes the spark. It stays still on top of the cylinder.

bricks.hint: Which part is joined straight to the piston?
bricks.explanation: The pistons push the **crankshaft** round, just as your legs push the pedals. Up-and-down pushes become a spin.

bricks.prompt: The engine is running and the crankshaft is spinning, but the gearbox is broken and passes nothing on. What happens?

options.text: The engine runs, but the wheels stay still
The car drives, but it's stuck in one gear
options.feedback: The gearbox is how the spin gets to the wheels. If it passes nothing on, the wheels get no spin at all.
The bangs happen in the engine, before the gearbox. The engine keeps going; its spin just can't reach the wheels.

bricks.hint: Follow the spin: piston, crankshaft, gearbox, wheels. Where does it stop?
bricks.explanation: The spin travels piston, crankshaft, gearbox, wheels. With the gearbox passing nothing on, the engine keeps running but the wheels never get turned.

bricks.prompt: Sort each moment by the gear the car needs.

items.text: Starting off when the traffic light turns green
Pulling away from the school gate
Going fast on a long, flat road
Cruising home on a flat, empty road

bricks.hint: Low gears give lots of push. When does the car need the most push?
bricks.explanation: Starting off and climbing need lots of push, so they use low gears. Going fast on a flat road needs speed, not push, so it uses high gears.

bricks.prompt: Sam drew how the engine's push gets to the wheels. Tap the part that doesn't belong.

bricks.hint: What does the exhaust pipe carry? Is it a spin?
bricks.explanation: The exhaust pipe only lets used-up gas out. The spin goes from the crankshaft to the **gearbox**, then to the wheels.

challenge.prompt: A car's spark plugs stop working. What happens when the driver tries to drive off?

options.text: No bangs, so nothing pushes the pistons and the wheels don't turn
The car still drives, but only in a low gear
options.feedback: Gears only pass on the spin the engine makes. With no bangs, there's no spin to pass on, in any gear.

options.text: The car still drives, but more slowly
options.feedback: Every push comes from a bang. Without sparks there are no bangs at all, so there are no pushes, not just weaker ones.

options.text: The fuel burns, but the used-up gas can't get out
options.feedback: The spark is what makes the fuel burn. No spark means nothing burns, so there's no gas to blow out.

challenge.hint: Which step needs the spark? What does that step do for the piston?
challenge.explanation: No spark means no bang. Without bangs nothing pushes the pistons, so the crankshaft, gearbox, and wheels get no spin.

takeaways: A petrol engine repeats four steps: suck, squeeze, bang, blow.
Only the bang gives a push: it shoves the piston down, and the piston turns the crankshaft.
The gearbox passes the spin to the wheels: low gears to start and climb, high gears to go fast.
